# SOP-P3-L3-05 Planned shutdown - Machining line

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P3, line P3-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, EQ-P3-L3-HP03  
Related documents: SB-1005, SB-1022, SOP-P3-L3-03

Purpose
1. Define the controlled sequence for a planned full shutdown of the Machining line to allow maintenance, inspection, and safe isolation of equipment EQ-P3-L3-SB01, EQ-P3-L3-CN02, and EQ-P3-L3-HP03.

Background and scope
2. This procedure applies to the Machining line in P3-L3 during planned outages where systems will be taken out of service for maintenance tasks that require zero-energy state and mechanical safeguarding. The procedure provides rationale for each step, examples of common maintenance activities, and the mandatory records to be completed.

Preconditions (must be verified before starting)
3. Confirm supervisory authorization for the planned shutdown and scope of work as recorded on the shutdown permit. Verify that affected production schedules have been updated and that downstream departments are notified. Confirm that required spares and tools for the planned tasks are available.

Personal protective equipment (PPE)
4. Mandatory PPE for personnel on the shutdown team: safety helmet, eye protection, hearing protection, cut-resistant gloves, and high-visibility clothing. Additional PPE for hydraulic and heavy mechanical work should be identified by the maintenance supervisor based on the task.

Shutdown sequence and steps
5. Step 1 — Initial controls and isolation
   - Notify operators and control room that shutdown is commencing.
   - Place machine controls in manual and stop automatic feeds.
   - Lockout and tagout electrical supply at the line main disconnect and to each equipment item following the site LOTO standard referenced in SB-1005.

6. Step 2 — Hydraulic isolation for EQ-P3-L3-HP03
   - Isolate hydraulic power to EQ-P3-L3-HP03 and relieve residual pressure per the hydraulic isolation instructions in SB-1022.
   - The system pressure limit for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 295 bar.
   - Verify pressure gauges read zero or are at ambient before opening any hydraulic connections.

7. Step 3 — Mechanical safety
   - Apply mechanical blocks or cribbing to secure movable masses where required for disassembly.
   - De-energize stored energy devices and secure accumulators according to manufacturer guidance.

8. Step 4 — Fastener control for EQ-P3-L3-HP03 main ram
   - When access for main ram removal or adjustment is required, follow the documented torque and fastener sequences.
   - The main ram bolt torque for Machining hydraulic forging press #3 (EQ-P3-L3-HP03) is 1600 N·m.
   - Use calibrated torque equipment and record the calibration tag reference in the maintenance record.

9. Step 5 — Component removal and inspection
   - Remove covers, guards, and service panels in the order described in SOP-P3-L3-03 to maintain structural integrity.
   - Inspect hydraulic fittings, seals, and structural welds for wear and record findings with photographs attached to the work order.

10. Step 6 — Example maintenance tasks
    - Example A: Replace or reseal a hydraulic cylinder on EQ-P3-L3-HP03 after verifying system is depressurized per SB-1022.
    - Example B: Replace sensor housings on EQ-P3-L3-SB01 with the machine mechanically blocked and electrical lockout applied.
    - For each example, list components removed, serial or tag numbers, and disposition (replaced, reconditioned, scrapped).

11. Step 7 — Pre-start checks and reassembly
    - Reinstall guards and covers in the reverse order of removal. Verify torque values using calibrated tools and record applied torque where specified.
    - Re-pressurize hydraulic systems slowly and verify there are no leaks at fittings or hoses before returning to full operating pressure.

Step rationale
12. Each step is designed to progressively remove energy and provide positive isolation to prevent inadvertent movement or release of stored energy. Isolation of hydraulics before mechanical intervention prevents fluid-driven movement. Controlling bolt torque on the main ram preserves structural clamping and prevents catastrophic failure under load; the specified torque is mandatory to achieve the designed clamping preload.

Records to keep
13. For each shutdown, file the following in the maintenance system:
    - Completed shutdown permit and authorization form.
    - Lockout/tagout checklist and signed LOTO tags.
    - Pressure gauge readings before and after hydraulic isolation.
    - Torque application records showing applied torque for the main ram bolt on EQ-P3-L3-HP03 and the calibration reference for the torque wrench used.
    - Inspection reports with photographic evidence and corrective action notes.
    - Post-maintenance test results and operator handover checklist.

Examples of record entries
14. Example entry: “Hydraulic isolation complete; gauge reads ambient; main ram bolt torque checked with calibrated wrench, applied torque as per spec recorded; no leaks detected during 15-minute pressurization hold.” Attach images of gauges and torque tool calibration label.

Return to service and verification
15. Conduct stepwise re-energization and verify functions at controlled settings. Confirm that safety interlocks and guards operate correctly and that no abnormal noises, leaks, or alarms are present. Complete a functional test run at operator station and obtain operator and maintenance sign-off before releasing equipment back to production.

Sign-off
16. The following signatures are required on the completed shutdown package:
   - Maintenance supervisor (name and signature)
   - Production supervisor (name and signature)
   - Safety representative (name and signature)
   - Date and time of handover to operations

Related documents and references
17. Consult SB-1005 for site lockout/tagout policy, SB-1022 for hydraulic isolation procedures, and SOP-P3-L3-03 for machine-specific disassembly and reassembly sequences.

Revision control
18. Maintain this procedure in the document control system and attach the completed shutdown package for auditing and continuous improvement.
